text.p: Fibreboard Corp said Monday it has finalized a five-year, $250 million unsecured credit agreement replacing the company's $150 million secured facility.

This new facility continues a $25 million five-year term loan associated with Vytec Corp, Fibreboard's Canadian vinyl siding manufacturing company. Its interest rate will vary from LIBOR plus 0.35 percent to LIBOR plus 0.875 percent.
The increased credit positions Fibreboard for expansion through internal growth and acquisitions within the building products industry, the company said.

"Currently, we are proceeding with the acquisition of Fabwel, a leader in key segments of the building products industry, for approximately $120 million. Our vinyl siding manufacturing plans call for increasing our total capacity by approximately 40 percent in 1997 including our new vinyl siding manufacturing plant in Joplin, Mo.," Fibreboard said.

"Additionally, we expect to significantly increase the production capacity of Stone Products Corp, the market leader in the cast stone industry, and add 15 new distribution centers in our exterior building products distribution business."
The bulk of this financing will be used for acquisition purposes for further opportunities in the building products sector, the company said.

The $250 million credit facility is headed by co-agents Bank of America and NationsBank and also includes ABM Amro Bank, Wells Fargo Bank, Texas Commerce Bank, Bank of Nova Scotia, Sanwa Bank California and U.S. Bank of Oregon.
